routes.speaker: John Ferrer

bridges.statement: Establish that morality ultimately requires God.
Show that objective moral facts require a divine truth-maker.
Show that reliable moral knowledge requires resources beyond a naturalistically produced brain.
Show that Christian ethics supplies a fuller explanatory and practical moral framework.

routes.position: God is required as the ultimate ground of morality

routes.speaker: Matt Dillahunty

bridges.statement: Establish that morality can be understood and practiced without God.
Ground moral assessment in consequences for well-being relative to shared goals.
Defend reason, evidence, and independent confirmation as publicly usable ways to improve moral knowledge.
Explain moral motivation and social cooperation without divine commands.

routes.position: Morality can be understood and practiced without God
